Optional. The DB schema enforces `headway_secs > 0` so this can't panic in production, but the function doesn't document that assumption and a unit test passing
`gtfsdb.Frequency{HeadwaySecs: 0}` directly would still hit it. A guard makes the
invariant explicit:

```suggestion
		headway := time.Duration(frequency.HeadwaySecs) * time.Second
		window := time.Duration(frequency.EndTime - frequency.StartTime)
		if headway == 0 {
			continue
		}
		runs += int(window / headway)
```

Not blocking.

Carry-forward note (pre-existing in the removed `fetchRouteRefs`): CLAUDE.md says to use
`route.AgencyID` rather than the stop's agency when forming combined route IDs, since a
stop can be served by routes from other agencies. `route.AgencyID` is available in the
loop. For single-agency feeds this makes no difference, so not blocking now, but worth
fixing before a multi-agency feed is added:

```suggestion
		combinedRouteID := utils.FormCombinedID(route.AgencyID, route.ID)
```

The refactor is well-structured: replacing the three parallel maps with a single `directionScheduleGroup` accumulator makes the new frequency path easy to add and the existing headsign-vote logic easier to follow. The frequency spec steps are correctly implemented. References staying populated on no-service dates matches Java (live-verified on Unitrans). Two optional defensive notes inline; everything else looks good.
